notes.title: Patchnotes: Patch 0.7.0 Alpha 1
notes.notes:
[h3][b]A Note Before We Begin[/b][/h3][p]We want to thank all players who have followed, supported, and tested beyond.frontiers over the past months.[/p][p]After a period of stepping back and restructuring internally, we're launching a new series of patches that lay the foundation for [b]Version 0.7.0[/b]. Many systems have been reworked or rebuilt entirely to improve long-term stability, performance, and scalability.[/p][p]The first transitional patch is now live. For now, only the [b]"Garden" system[/b] is available as we test and stabilize the new core. More content and systems will follow shortly - with new team members aboard, our update pace is set to increase significantly.[/p][p][b][i][u]Important Notes on This Phase:[/u][/i][/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Old saves are no longer compatible.[/b]
Due to major internal changes, a full reset is necessary.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Progress is currently not persistent.[/b]
While we’re migrating core systems like saving, inventory, and sector states, [b]save data will not be stored[/b].[/p][/*][*][p][b]Stability is the top priority.[/b] The frequent crashes and technical issues from the 0.5.x patch series, especially after the chat server went down should now be resolved.[/p][/*][/list][p]We welcome your feedback on this new foundation on the game's [url="https://discord.beyondfrontiers.eu" style="button"]Discord Server[/url]. It will help shape [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] into the game it deserves to become. More patches are already in the works.[/p][p]We know the wait for this update has been long, and we won’t sugarcoat the delay. Development was invisible while we reassessed the entire structure of the game - both technically and design-wise. What emerged is a glimpse of [i]UNDAUNTED[/i]; a rebuild that took into account nearly all player feedback and bug reports, over half a year of work. Instead of patching over problems, we’ve restructured beyond.frontiers from the ground up, aiming for long-term maintainability and clarity of vision.[/p][p]We're also thrilled to officially welcome four new crew members aboard the [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] development train: [b]Chael[/b] and [b]Sana[/b], our talented story writers, who will help bring deeper narrative arcs and lore to life; [b]Rosy[/b], joining us as our new UI/UX artist, working to reshape the interface into something both beautiful and functional; and [b]ManedWolf[/b], stepping in as our Audio and Music Coordinator, crafting the soundscapes and musical identity of the universe. With their combined strengths, we're better equipped than ever to push [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] into its next era.[/p][h2][b]New Features - Core Systems[/b][/h2][h3][b]Character Creation Reimagined[/b][/h3][p]The first time you start a new game in [i]UNDAUNTED[/i], you'll notice that character creation is no longer a placeholder. It’s been fully redesigned into a streamlined but meaningful introduction to your journey.[/p][p][b]New options include:[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Body Type Selection
[/b]Choose from multiple body types to visually represent your commander. (This currently has no gameplay impact but will affect future portrait rendering and profile systems.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Commander Name 
[/b]Choose your callsign and identity. Used for in-game comms, save slots, and future log-based features.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Preferred Pronouns 
[/b]Set how you are referred to across all NPC interactions and interfaces. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Faction Selection (6 Total) 
[/b]Choose one of [b]six unique factions[/b], each with its own starting location, narrative context, and reputation implications:[/p][list][*][p]Three factions are available from the start[/p][/*][*][p][b]Three additional factions are unlockable[/b] through gameplay milestones and discoveries[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Starter Ship Selection (3 Options)
[/b]Begin your journey with one of three starter-class ships:[/p][list][*][p][b]Starlite[/b] - The classic all-rounder and default option[/p][/*][*][p][b]Syf[/b] - A compact mining vessel, optimized for early resource gathering and durability[/p][/*][*][p][b]Arcos[/b] - A light freighter focused on trade, storage capacity, and efficiency in bulk hauling[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]Each choice defines your early-game location, available tasks, and your position within the evolving economy and faction landscape.[/p][h2][b]New Features - Universe & Navigation[/b][/h2][h3][b]20× Larger Sectors[/b][/h3][p]The playable universe has undergone a complete transformation. Sector dimensions have been increased by a factor of [b]twenty[/b], creating a sense of scale and distance that more accurately reflects the tone and intended pacing of [i]beyond.frontiers[/i].[/p][list][*][p]Distances now matter: sectors are no longer compact zones but vast regions with traversal requirements.[/p][/*][*][p]Stations, asteroid fields, and anomalies are placed with more purpose and separation, encouraging navigation planning.[/p][/*][*][p]Sensor ranges, signal degradation, and visibility are recalibrated to fit the new spatial scale. [/p][/*][/list][p]This change lays the foundation for more meaningful exploration, long-distance missions, and isolated deep-space encounters in future updates.[/p][h3][b]Hyperlane Travel System[/b][/h3][p]To support the expanded scale and enable efficient long-range travel, a new [b]Hyperlane Network[/b] has been introduced. These are high-speed transit corridors linking key locations across a sector.[/p][list][*][p]Hyperlanes allow significantly faster movement between major stations, gates, and landmarks.[/p][/*][*][p]Ships remain vulnerable while traveling; hyperlane ambushes and piracy are possible in contested regions.[/p][/*][*][p]Manual travel outside of hyperlanes remains viable, but comes at the cost of time.[/p][/*][/list][p]This system addresses the practical needs of scale and player agency.[/p][h3][b]Revised Ship Scaling & Presence[/b][/h3][p]All ships in the game - player and NPC - have been rescaled to better reflect their physical mass and in-universe purpose. This brings visual clarity and physical weight to every encounter.[/p][list][*][p][b]Fighter-class ships[/b] remain small and agile, with realistic proportions in relation to stations and capital ships.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Freighters and industrial vessels[/b] now occupy more screen space and require more deliberate piloting.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Capital ships[/b] and station-class constructs are now massive in scope and harder to ignore.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Stations[/b] have been massively resized to also reflect this rescaling making them look like huge behemoths housing millions of people[/p][/*][*][p]Collision, docking alignment, and visual parallax have all been adjusted to accommodate the new scaling system.[/p][/*][/list][p]Combined with the larger sectors and hyperlane infrastructure, this brings the game world closer to its intended visual and navigational identity.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]New Features - Planetary Content (Foundational Implementation)[/b][/h2][h3][b]Landfall: Surface-Level Planetary Exploration[/b][/h3][p]As part of the long-term expansion of the game world, [i]UNDAUNTED[/i] introduces the [b]first stage of planetary surface content[/b]. Many planets across the galaxy can now be [b]visited, landed on, and traversed[/b] to varying degrees.[/p][p]This system is still in early development but forms the platform for a much broader set of features in future updates.[/p][p][b]Key Features Now Implemented:[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Multiple landable planets per sector[/b], each with their own surface maps and unique terrain profiles[/p][/*][*][p]Surface environments vary in detail, representing deserts, grassy surfaces or other places,[/p][/*][*][p]Landfall sites are currently limited to predefined locations, but more dynamic systems are in development[/p][/*][/list][p][b]What This Enables Going Forward:[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Faction-controlled planetary settlements
[/b] Planned for future updates: facilities, garrisons, and economic hubs tied to territory control[/p][/*][*][p][b]Exploration mechanics
[/b] Environmental hazards, hidden resources, crash sites, and deep-surface anomalies[/p][/*][*][p][b]Player-founded cities and colonies
[/b] A long-term goal: players establishing cities that generate [b]resources[/b], [b]station influence[/b], or [b]tax income[/b] over time[/p][/*][/list][p]Planetary content is not yet a core gameplay loop - but with [i]UNDAUNTED[/i], it now exists in-engine and can grow alongside player progression and factional conflict.[/p][h2][b]New Features - Interface & User Experience[/b][/h2][h3][b]Fully Modular UI System[/b][/h3][p]The user interface has been entirely rewritten from the ground up. What was once static and rigid is now dynamic, scalable, and responsive. The new system introduces [b]modular, movable windows[/b] that adapt to your screen, your control method, and your workflow.[/p][p][b]Key Features:[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]All major UI panels[/b] (inventory, map, status, missions, ship info, trade, etc.) can now be moved and repositioned freely[/p][/*][*][p][b]Drag-and-drop interaction[/b] supported across all inventory and ship management elements[/p][/*][*][p]Clean visual style with improved font rendering, spacing, and icon clarity[/p][/*][*][p][b]Layered UI logic[/b] prevents windows from overlapping critical ship information in-flight[/p][/*][/list][p]This marks a major usability improvement - especially for players who want to personalize their command interface or run the game in unconventional resolutions or aspect ratios.[/p][h3][b]
Translation-Ready Interface[/b][/h3][p]In addition to structural changes, the entire UI is now connected to a [b]runtime translation layer[/b].[/p][list][*][p]All visible interface text can now be localized without rebuilding the game[/p][/*][*][p]Language selection is available directly from the in-game options menu[/p][/*][*][p]Future community-supported language packs are possible through dragging and dropping new translations into the Lang Folder[/p][/*][*][p]Internal fallback and debug modes included for development and testing[/p][/*][/list][p]This is the final foundational system needed to make beyond.frontiers accessible to a broader audience - and a core step toward long-term support.[/p][h2][b]New Features - World Generation & Custom Editing[/b][/h2][h3][b]Rewritten World Generation System[/b][/h3][p][i]UNDAUNTED[/i] introduces a completely rebuilt [b]WorldGen system[/b], designed for greater performance, modularity, and stability across all configurations.[/p][p][b]Key Improvements:[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Distance-aware sector loading
[/b] The engine now generates and loads only the content nearest to the player’s current location. This drastically reduces memory usage and avoids unnecessary background processing.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Black Screen Bug Resolved
[/b] Reports of long loading times or permanent black screens during sector initialization have been addressed by this system. Initialization is now tied to proximity, not full-sector state.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Optimized for Scale
[/b] Despite already being lightweight by modern standards, the new system further reduces CPU and memory impact, particularly when navigating between sparsely populated or empty systems.[/p][/*][/list][p]This foundation ensures the galaxy can continue to grow without burdening player machines, and prepares the engine for future features such as dynamic encounters, procedural anomalies, and scripted location spawning.[/p][h3][b]All-New Level Editor[/b][/h3][p]A powerful [b]sector editing tool[/b] is now included in the game, giving players direct control over their own universe.[/p][p][b]Editor Capabilities:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Modify existing sectors to fit your preferred gameplay style[/p][/*][*][p]Add, reposition, or remove stations, planets, gates, and trade points[/p][/*][*][p]Fine-tune distances, scale, lighting conditions, and object relationships[/p][/*][*][p]Save and reload your own modified sector layouts with minimal effort[/p][/*][*][p]Designed to match the same internal structure used by the game’s core worldbuilder[/p][/*][/list][p]This tool allows players to shape the game’s universe in a way that suits their strategies - whether that means creating a densely populated trade zone, a remote pirate haven, or a clean-slate exploration sector.[/p][p]The editor does not require external software and runs inside the engine, using the same assets and logic as the live game.[/p][h2][b]New Features - Resources & Asteroid Economy[/b][/h2][h3][b]High-Definition Asteroids[/b][/h3][p]Asteroid visuals have been overhauled with [b]new high-resolution models[/b], significantly improving environmental detail across all asteroid belts and mining zones.[/p][list][*][p]Updated mesh detail and lighting interaction[/p][/*][*][p]Improved collision geometry for smoother navigation[/p][/*][*][p]Asteroid fields now appear more physically varied and visually dense, even at long distances[/p][/*][/list][p]In addition, [b]six new asteroid objects [/b]have been introduced - empty rock types without resource nodes - to bring natural variation and more believable belt composition. This helps differentiate between rich and barren fields during both visual scanning and sensor analysis.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]New Resource Materials[/b][/h3][p][i]UNDAUNTED[/i] introduces a [b]completely new set of mineable materials[/b], each with distinct properties, rarity, and value. These resources replace the previous generic ore types and are now tied directly into the economic and crafting systems.[/p][p][b]New Materials:[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Ferriscarlet[/b] - A dense, iron-heavy core material used in industrial ship frames[/p][/*][*][p][b]Noctium[/b] - A volatile black mineral found in deeper belts; key to energy shielding components[/p][/*][*][p][b]Aurivite[/b] - Gold-alloyed trace mineral, high in trade value and used in sensor fabrication[/p][/*][*][p][b]Paleon[/b] - A fibrous, pale lattice mineral found on the edge of dead systems; vital for high-end electronics[/p][/*][*][p][b]Crythene[/b] - Crystalized methane-infused ice, used in ship fuel systems and advanced coolant technologies[/p][/*][/list][p]Each material features a [b]unique visual appearance[/b], making it easier to identify in the field without relying solely on scanners. They replace the old Minerals.[/p][h3][b]Rescaled Mining Economy[/b][/h3][p]Alongside the new materials, the [b]entire mining and trading economy will be recalibrated[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]Ore yields now vary by asteroid type and extraction efficiency[/p][/*][*][p]Material values have been rebalanced to reflect rarity, utility, and trade demand[/p][/*][*][p]Industrial missions and trade routes will be updated to include the new resources[/p][/*][*][p]Future updates will expand crafting and production systems based on this new resource tier[/p][/*][/list][p]This rescale provides a more meaningful progression path for miners, traders, and industrial players - making material choice and extraction location part of long-term strategy.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]New Features - Starter Ships[/b][/h2][h3][b]Two New Entry-Class Ships[/b][/h3][p]The [i]UNDAUNTED[/i] update introduces two all-new starter-class vessels alongside the classic Starlite. Each is designed to support a specific early-game playstyle and provide more meaningful choices at the beginning of a new session.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Arcos - Entry-Level Trade Ship[/b][/h3][p]Originally designed as a compact bomber hull, the [b]Arcos[/b] has been refitted into a [b]streamlined, fast courier and trading ship[/b] - perfect for players interested in economic gameplay over direct combat.[/p][p][b]Key Characteristics:[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]High cargo capacity[/b] relative to its small frame[/p][/*][*][p][b]Superior engine efficiency and acceleration[/b], ideal for fast docking and escape routes[/p][/*][*][p][b]Reduced weapon systems[/b], reflecting its retrofit away from combat toward commerce[/p][/*][*][p]Built for players who prefer trade, hauling, and logistics over direct engagement[/p][/*][/list][p]Its agility and speed make it a strong early choice for missions that require fast delivery or high-risk navigation through disputed sectors; but its limited firepower demands caution.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Syf - Entry-Level Mining Vessel[/b][/h3][p]The [b]Syf[/b] is a uniquely shaped, [b]disc-profile mining vessel[/b] equipped with specialized hardpoints for resource extraction. Its visual silhouette sets it apart from any other starter ship, and its systems are optimized for early industrial gameplay.[/p][p][b]Key Characteristics:[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Reinforced hull and shielding[/b], built to survive long sessions in asteroid fields[/p][/*][*][p][b]Compact form factor[/b] allows for nimble maneuvering in dense terrain[/p][/*][/list][p]The Syf is ideal for players looking to build their economic foundation through mining and resource transport, while remaining self-sufficient early on.[/p][p]With these two additions, [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] now offers three distinct paths from the start - Combat (Starlite), Industry (Syf), and Trade (Arcos) - each with its own strategy, challenges, and eventual upgrades.[/p][h2][b]New Features - Combat, AI & Player Systems[/b][/h2][h3][b]Reputation System Overhaul[/b][/h3][p]The old vague standing system has been replaced with a fully numeric, transparent [b]0-1000 reputation scale[/b]. Every faction now tracks your status with precise values that dynamically shift based on your actions, affiliations, and mission performance.[/p][p][b]Reputation Levels (Ascending):[/b][/p][list][*][p]0–149: [b]Hated[/b][/p][/*][*][p]150–299: [b]Disliked[/b][/p][/*][*][p]300–449: [b]Tolerated[/b][/p][/*][*][p]450–549: [b]Neutral[/b][/p][/*][*][p]550–699: [b]Liked[/b][/p][/*][*][p]700–899: [b]Favoured[/b][/p][/*][*][p]900–1000: [b]Ally[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]Reputation now affects[/p][list][*][p]Access to restricted sectors[/p][/*][*][p]Trade route pricing and taxation[/p][/*][*][p]Station docking permissions[/p][/*][*][p]Mission availability and risk scaling[/p][/*][*][p]AI response time during conflict or emergencies[/p][/*][/list][p]This provides a clearer, more readable progression path for players seeking to align with (or betray) factions across the galaxy.[/p][h3][b]TOASt AI Upgrade  Tactical Output & Adaptive Simulation Technology[/b][/h3][p]The [b]TOASt AI system[/b] has been refined to provide [b]more reactive and varied NPC behavior[/b] in combat and patrol routines.[/p][p][b]Improvements Include:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Smarter positional awareness in asteroid fields and around structures[/p][/*][*][p]Prioritized targeting logic (based on threat, hull class, and distance)[/p][/*][*][p]Aggression modulation based on player standing and faction rulesets[/p][/*][*][p]Better formation handling and mid-combat decision-making[/p][/*][/list][p]Expect patrols, pirates, and convoys to respond more dynamically, and sometimes unpredictably based on local sector conditions.[/p][h3][b]Expanded Weapon Systems[/b][/h3][p][i]UNDAUNTED[/i] brings a much-needed expansion to the weapon ecosystem, adding variety and tactical decision-making.[/p][p][b]Weapon Types Introduced:[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Beam Weapons
[/b] High damage, pinpoint accuracy, and long range. Best used in controlled bursts.
 - [b]Strength:[/b] Devastating impact on single targets
 - [b]Tradeoff:[/b] Long cooldown and high energy draw
[/p][/*][*][p][b]Projectile Weapons
[/b] Fast-firing, fast-traveling kinetic weapons. Ideal for high-speed dogfights.
 - [b]Strength:[/b] Rapid output and easier tracking
 - [b]Tradeoff:[/b] Lower individual shot damage and limited effectiveness on large hulls
[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mining Lasers (Universal)
[/b] Previously limited to mining ships, [b]mining lasers can now be equipped on any ship[/b] via standard weapon slots.
 - All ships can now participate in mining
 - However, only [b]dedicated mining vessels[/b] (like the Syf) receive [b]yield bonuses[/b] and [b]material difficulty reduction
[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]Everything listed above represents only the [b]most visible layer[/b] of what [i]UNDAUNTED[/i] brings to beyond.frontiers. Below the surface, you'll find a wealth of other improvements and additions:[/p][list][*][p][b]New space background sets[/b], enhancing visual depth and regional identity[/p][/*][*][p]Early implementation of [b]physical collision simulations[/b] for improved realism during docking, combat, and object interactions[/p][/*][*][p]The introduction of [b]3D planets[/b] in the visual layer, replacing flat background textures with rotating planetary bodies[/p][/*][*][p]Dozens of backend optimizations and structural changes designed to reduce load times, improve stability, and future-proof the engine[/p][/*][/list][p]We want to be clear: [b]not everything on our wishlist has made it into the initial 0.7.0 release[/b]. Some features have been deferred to ensure overall stability, and others are waiting on technical dependencies that were only just completed.[/p][p]However, if this update proves as stable in the wild as it has in testing, we expect to [b]accelerate development significantly[/b] from here onward.[/p][h2][b]Changes & Improvements[/b][/h2][h3][b]Asteroid System Reworked[/b][/h3][p]The outdated static asteroid fields have been fully removed. In their place, [i]UNDAUNTED[/i] introduces a [b]dynamic asteroid spawning system[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]Asteroid belts and scrap fields now generate [b]decorative debris dynamically[/b], based on player position and visibility[/p][/*][*][p]Reduces visual clutter and improves performance across large sectors[/p][/*][*][p]Ensures that belts feel more alive, varied, and worth revisiting[/p][/*][*][p]Resource-rich asteroids remain persistent, while background elements adapt in real time[/p][/*][/list][p]This makes navigating belts and scrap zones [b]feel like active environments[/b] instead of passive scenery.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Station Access Now Tied to Reputation[/b][/h3][p]Docking access is no longer universal. Stations may now [b]deny docking clearance[/b] if your reputation with their controlling faction is too low.[/p][list][*][p]Access thresholds vary by faction and security level[/p][/*][*][p]Reputation growth is now essential for trade, mission access, and navigation rights[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Energy-Linked Equipment Limits[/b][/h3][p]To curb over-stacking of high-end modules, [i]UNDAUNTED[/i] will introduce [b]energy limits on all ships[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]Every piece of active equipment now draws from your ship’s energy pool[/p][/*][*][p]Overloading your ship will result in [b]disabled systems[/b], reduced weapon uptime, or even forced shutdowns[/p][/*][*][p]Encourages smarter loadouts and role-focused ship design over brute stacking[/p][/*][/list][p]This change adds tactical depth and better balances early vs. late-game progression.[/p][h3][b]Faction Logos Fully Remade[/b][/h3][p]All faction insignia have been redesigned to reflect their current lore, color language, and aesthetic identity.[/p][list][*][p]High-resolution logos are now used across UI panels, communications, and system maps[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Ship Hangar Limit Increased[/b][/h3][p]Players can [b]own and store up to 40 ships[/b] in their personal hangar.[/p][list][*][p]Additional categories and visual markers will be added in upcoming patches[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Sector Reclassification: Luna, Kurai, Scire[/b][/h3][p]These three core systems have been reclassified as [b]backwater safety sectors[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]Designed for new players, neutral encounters, and non-hostile mission testing[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced patrol aggression, no large hostile spawns, and slower economic fluctuation[/p][/*][*][p]Reputation loss and gain occur more slowly in these sectors to allow experimentation without major penalty[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Global Ship Rebalancing[/b][/h3][p]Numerous ships have been rebalanced in terms of:[/p][list][*][p][b]Weapon hardpoints[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Maneuverability and mass[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Energy output and consumption[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Cargo and upgrade slots[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]Changes aim to reinforce ship roles, eliminate exploit loadouts, and increase variety in early-game choices.[/p][h2][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/h2][p]We’ll be honest - [b]the number of bugs fixed in UNDAUNTED is difficult to quantify[/b].[/p][p]Between the complete rewrites of world generation, UI systems, AI behavior, and core game logic, many older issues simply no longer exist in the same form. Some bugs were rendered obsolete by design changes, others were discovered deep within legacy systems and quietly removed during cleanup.[/p][p]What we can say is this:[/p][list][*][p][b]The black screen bug[/b] during sector load has been resolved through the new distance-aware WorldGen[/p][/*][*][p][b]AI patrol logic bugs[/b], such as circling indefinitely or failing to respond to player attacks, have been rewritten entirely under the TOASt system[/p][/*][*][p][b]Inventory stack corruption[/b] and disappearing equipment edge-cases have been addressed[/p][/*][*][p][b]Asteroid belt LOD and collision issues[/b] are resolved under the dynamic spawning system[/p][/*][*][p][b]Docking bugs[/b], such as softlocks or animation freezes, should no longer occur[/p][/*][*][p][b]UI scaling and text clipping errors[/b] are gone due to the modular windowing rewrite[/p][/*][*][p][b]Ghost ships, phantom pings, and persistent mission markers[/b] have all been systematically hunted down[/p][/*][/list][p]We’ve also fixed dozens of smaller, unlisted bugs reported by community testers - and we’re incredibly grateful for every report that led us to a fix.[/p][p]Please note that this version still contains a number of known issues. The migration to [b]NUI3[/b], our new in-house UI plugin, is still in progress; some menus may look inconsistent, and several elements are still relying on legacy code. You’ll also encounter [b]placeholder graphics[/b], especially in early game screens, and [b]incomplete translations[/b] across various languages. These are actively being addressed in the upcoming patch cycle, but we wanted to bring the updated foundation into your hands early to begin gathering feedback and further stabilize the systems under live conditions.[/p][h2][b]Closing Words – A Milestone Reached[/b][/h2][p]When [i]UNDAUNTED[/i] [b][u]fully[/u][/b] releases, it will mark the culmination of [b]over a year of dedicated, often exhausting work[/b].[/p][p]This update was a complete structural rebuild of [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] across almost every layer. From how the game starts, to how sectors are loaded, to how windows move, to how reputations shift and ships fire; everything was re-examined, rewritten, or replaced.[/p][p]We paused updates not because the project was on hold, but because we knew that [b]quick patches weren’t enough[/b]. To carry [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] forward, we had to make it sustainable, scalable, and stable. That meant solving long-standing problems instead of working around them.[/p][p]We’re now confident that the version we’re releasing is worthy of a paper relaunch and we genuinely hope that it [b]works out of the box[/b], performs well, and sets the standard for what comes next.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]beyond.frontiers at POLARIS 2025[/b][/h2][p]We’re also proud to announce that [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] has been [b]officially invited to exhibit at the Indie Arena Booth at POLARIS 2025[/b] in Hamburg. This will be our [b]first public convention appearance[/b], and the first time the [i]UNDAUNTED[/i] build is shown live to a broader audience.[/p][p]If you're attending, you’ll be able to:[/p][list][*][p]Play the current full version of [i]beyond.frontiers[/i][/p][/*][*][p]Meet some of the development team in person[/p][/*][*][p]Receive goodies both for Ingame and Real World[/p][/*][*][p]And - while supplies last - claim a [b]boxed physical edition[/b] including:[/p][list][*][p]A limited boxed copy of the game.[/p][/*][*][p]A [b]limited "Polaris Star" skin DLC[/b] for the Starlite, Arcos and Syf ships[/p][/*][*][p][b]Exclusively available for free at Polaris[/b][/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]To claim a boxed edition, just bring your [b]Discord username[/b] and the [b]codeword[/b] (to be revealed in the weeks before the event).[/p][p]Thank you for sticking with us. Whether you’ve been following since the earliest builds or you’re discovering [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] for the first time, we’re excited to share what’s next.[/p][p]More to come.[/p][p]- The Duality Beyond Studios Team[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: A Preview to Patch 0.6.0 – UNDAUNTED
notes.notes:
[b]After a longer period of silence, we’d like to share an update on the current state and direction of beyond.frontiers.[/b]

Over the past months, we have paused regular public updates to perform a thorough technical overhaul of the project. This decision was made following our visit to Revision 2025, where we gathered significant feedback and input from other developers and creators. Much of it challenged the foundation of the current game, which led us to revisit core systems, scope, and the planned feature roadmap.

We are now in active development of Patch 0.6.0, titled UNDAUNTED. The roadmap has been reset. No release estimate is available yet, but development will continue steadily, with new insights and previews to be shared on our Discord and YouTube channels in the coming weeks and months.

[h2]Planned Additions and Changes for Patch 0.6.0[/h2]
[h1]New Features:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Ship Scaling: Ships have been resized to better reflect their class and function, improving spatial consistency.
[*] Sector Scaling: Sector size has increased by a factor of 20 to allow for more exploration space.
[*] Station Scaling: Stations now scale proportionally to ship sizes, functioning more like small cities.
[*] Hyperlanes: System-internal fast-travel paths between key locations.
[*] New Ships: Two additional starter-class ships (Syf and Arcos) have been added.
[*] Revised Character Creation: Players will choose one of three ships when starting a new game.
[*] New Space Backgrounds: Visual variety has been expanded with additional high-resolution skyspheres.
[*] New World Generation: Procedural generation has been rewritten for improved structure and consistency.
[*] 3D Planets: The game now includes a selection of over 70 landable planetary types with new textures.
[*] Planet Surfaces: Certain planets will be explorable on foot or via land vehicles.
[/list]
and much, much more...

[h2]Features in Development:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Land Control: Factions will be able to claim and tax planetary surfaces.
[*] Planetary Cities: Cities serve as economic and production hubs under faction ownership.
[*] Atmospheric Entry: Gradual descent systems from space to planet surface.
[*] Sector Editor: Players will be able to create and customize their own sectors.
[*] Collision Simulation: A new physical system for handling collisions and docking behavior.
[*] Station Interiors: Ability to exit ships and navigate station environments.
[*] UI and System Improvements: New main menu, redesigned UI, and updated faction visuals.
[*] Expanded Hardware Support: Preliminary support planned for Controllers, VR, HOTAS, AudioLink, and Steam Deck.
[/list]

[h2]Changes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Skysphere Rotation: Backgrounds can now be rotated per sector for improved variance.
[*] Access Restrictions: Reputation now affects whether a player can dock at a station.
[*] Equipment System (EQP): Equipment slots now introduce progression mechanics via point-based limits.
[/list]

[h2]Fixes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Blank names and blackscreen bugs after jumping between systems have been resolved.
[/list]

[h2]Removed:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Station Company Ownerships: All stations are now owned by core factions. This change simplifies access logic and reputation tracking.
[/list]

[h1]Pricing Notice[/h1]
Due to shifts in development costs, environmental factors, and overall project scope, we plan to raise the price of beyond.frontiers in the near future to an average of 20$ to keep the development of beyond.frontiers running. The current pricing structure was set during a much earlier phase of development. With the growing complexity and long-term vision of the game, this adjustment is necessary to support ongoing work, infrastructure, and fair compensation for contributors.

We will continue to share development insights through our regular communication channels on Youtube and Discord. Thank you for your patience and interest in the project.

– The beyond.frontiers team

notes.title: Development Update - February 2025
notes.notes:
[b]Greetings Commanders,[/b]

I wanted to take a moment to talk about something important regarding our update schedule moving forward.

Since November 15th, I’ve been working at full capacity to keep these updates coming at a weekly pace. It’s been an incredible journey, and seeing the game grow with each patch has been amazing—but at the same time, it’s also been exhausting. Keeping up with weekly releases while managing everything else behind the scenes has started to take its toll, and I can feel the burnout slowly creeping in.

On top of that, February has been a tough month for sales, estimated under 100$ after fees and taxes. As much as we love working on this game, we still have to keep the lights on, which means taking on other jobs and projects to help sustain development. Balancing that with a weekly update schedule is becoming increasingly difficult, and we don’t want to end up in a situation where we have to rush things just to meet a deadline.

Because of this, we’ve decided to switch to a bi-weekly release schedule moving forward. This will give us more time to focus on delivering better, more polished updates instead of constantly crunching to get something out every seven days. It also means we can take care of ourselves a little better and ensure that we’re able to keep working on this game for the long run.

This doesn’t mean less content—if anything, it means we can take the time to refine what we’re adding and make sure every patch is truly worth the wait. It also gives us the breathing room to focus on bigger updates, improve existing systems, and take player feedback into account more thoroughly.

[b]How You Can Help[/b]
If you enjoy the game and want to see it continue to grow, the biggest way you can support us is by spreading the word. Share it with your friends, drop a review, recommend it to people who might enjoy it. Every new player helps us keep pushing forward.

We’ve also been thinking about ways to keep things sustainable in the long term. If there’s enough community interest, we could look into running a Kickstarter to help fund the game’s development more directly. That could even come with physical rewards like art prints, ship blueprints, or collector’s items for those who want to support at a higher level. If that’s something you’d be interested in, let us know!

We really appreciate all of you who have been supporting the game, whether by playing, giving feedback, or just being part of the community. It means a lot, and we want to make sure we’re doing right by you while also making sure we can keep this project going strong.

Thanks for understanding, and we’re excited to keep building this world with you! :rocket:

- Dex and the Team

notes.title: Version 0.4.3 - Little Things and Large Tasks

From my earliest programming experiments to building this very universe, Mark’s vision and ingenuity, his passion for development, they all have been a constant companion.

His engines empowered so many of us to create not just games but memories, careers, and communities. Losing him is a tremendous blow to us, but his legacy endures in every project born in his works. From BlitzBasic, to Monkey, we salute you. o7

notes.title: Patch Notes: 0.4.2b1 - Economic Consolidation
notes.notes:
[h2]Welcome to patch 0.4.2b1! [/h2]

ETA: Today, 29th Nov 2024

This update focuses on refining the game’s core mechanics, streamlining the economy for better player accessibility, and unleashing the full range of ships and equipment to expand your options as a privateer. Alongside these changes, we’ve made adjustments to starter systems, added hundreds of new rumors to immerse you in the universe, and scaled up key capital ships to give them the gravitas they deserve. Dive into the details below and explore the changes that will shape your journey in the stars!

[h2]New Features[/h2]
[h3]Condensed Economy[/h3]
After reviewing extensive feedback and gameplay footage, we've simplified the early-game economy:
Individual ore processing stations have been merged into two categories:
[list]
[*] Metal Refinery: Processes Iron, Copper, and Gold.
[*] Advanced Refinery: Handles Silicone and Uranium.
[/list]

Aside that, we did a major overhaul to the economy:
[list]
[*] Ice Directly Sold to Food Processors and the Station is moved to Tier 1.
[*] Tier 2 Station Reduction: Tier 2 production chains reduced from 9 stations to 5.
[*] Tier 3 Stations have been completely removed.
[/list]
This change aims to streamline resource flow and make the economy more intuitive for newer players.

[h3]Expanded Equipment and Ship Availability[/h3]
The entire ship roster is now accessible to players, including: Trade ships from the compact Demeter to the massive Atlas. Miners like the Keon and Gaius. Fighters such as the Starlite and Fury Heavy.
Many stations will now offer limited stock of certain ships, so share your discoveries in the forums or Discord.
⁠
[h3]New Equipment Added[/h3]

A wider variety of Weapons, Thrusters, Shields, and Utility modules are now available.
Expect minor nerfs to older gear to encourage the hunt for optimized builds.

[h3]GenAI Disabled by Default[/h3]

Character Images are now disabled by default.
You can re-enable them in the Options menu (this must be done every game start).
This is a temporary measure until real images can be added.

[h2]Changes[/h2]
[h3]Capital Ship Scaling[/h3]
The Crusader, Khyber, and Evoke have received size adjustments for greater visual impact and functionality:
[list]
[*] Crusader: Scaled up by 150%.
[*] Khyber and Evoke: Scaled up by 200%.
[/list]

[h3]Sector Updates[/h3]

Additional content has been added to certain sectors for a richer exploration experience.

[h3]Starter System Rework[/h3]

Each starter system now features a Food Processing Plant and an Ice Belt.
This allows players to mine, trade, or fight immediately after completing the tutorial without needing to search for buyers or resources.

[h3]Added 400 New Rumors[/h3]

A mix of true, false, and neutral rumors to further immerse players in the universe.

[h3]Game Internal Screenshot Key Removed[/h3]

Removed the internal screenshot key to avoid confusion with Steam Screenshot Function.

[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[b]Reputation Calculation Bug[/b]: Fixed an issue where faction reputation was calculated incorrectly if the player was not directly involved in events.
[b]Neutral Space Reputation[/b]: Removed unintended faction reputation changes when the player is in neutral space.

This update brings a major overhaul to the economy, expands ship and equipment access, and introduces a host of quality-of-life improvements. Happy piloting, and as always, your feedback is invaluable! 🚀

notes.title: 0.4.2 Alpha 1 - "A Death's a Death"
notes.notes:
[h1]Multiplayer Test Conclusion[/h1]
The Multiplayer Test has now officially ended, and we were thrilled by the turnout—over 1,800 players joined or attempted to connect. This marks an important milestone in our development journey, testing the limits of our networking features. We’re especially proud of the core performance, even though some connectivity issues, particularly with RDP Keepalives, presented challenges.

It's worth noting that our goal isn’t to create a massive MMO but rather to offer a more intimate multiplayer experience where players can host private servers and team up with friends. This allows for controlled, cooperative play within smaller groups, giving players autonomy in shaping their frontier adventures. Thank you to everyone who participated, provided feedback, and helped pave the way for our next steps. Multiplayer connectivity will be temporarily disabled with this update but will return with refined features in the upcoming 0.6.x patch series.

[h1]New Features[/h1]
[b]NPC Aggro System[/b]
NPCs can now detect, engage, and damage players. Both Crimewatch and Defensewatch systems are live, meaning player actions are now subject to faction-based consequences. Stay alert and watch your reputation!

[b]Player Ship Turrets[/b]
After resolving long-standing deletion issues, player ship turrets are fully functional. Equip your turrets and take advantage of enhanced firepower in hostile situations.

[b]NPC Turret Aggro[/b]
NPC ships with turrets now respond with aggressive behavior. Prepare for a more immersive, dynamic combat experience as NPC defenses are fortified.

[b]Shield and Armor Damage System[/b]
Incoming attacks now pause shield regeneration, adding a layer of strategy in combat. If armor is depleted to zero…

[b]Player Death, Rebuy, and Respawn Mechanic[/b]
…the player’s ship is destroyed, triggering a respawn option in the home system of your faction. Rebuy your ship with current equipment for 65% of its value. Demo Achievement holders receive a 15% discount on this rebuy option in the full game. Alternatively, players can respawn in a Starlite ship for free, though no modules are retained.

[b]Reputation Levels[/b]
Faction perception is now influenced by player actions, granting more depth to NPC interactions and alliances across the universe. Reputation impacts responses from factions, trading opportunities, and conflict likelihood.

[b]Radiation Damage[/b]
Certain systems and areas are now irradiated, damaging your hull over time. Approach with caution and ensure your defenses are adequate to withstand the environmental hazards.

[b]Achievements[/b]
An achievement system has been introduced, tracking player milestones, exploration, combat, and faction-related accomplishments. Progress is recorded in the player's profile, with achievements unlocking exclusive rewards and ship modifications in the future.

[b]Cloud Save System[/b]
Save game data is now synced to the cloud, ensuring that progress is preserved across multiple devices. Play confidently knowing your journey is backed up and available whenever you’re ready to jump back into the action.

[h1]Minor Fixes & Improvements[/h1]
[list]
[*] Reduced Volume on Mining Sounds for a less jarring experience.
[*] Additional AI Triggers for the Board Computer to cover missed actions.
[*] Resolved NPC Communication Issues where certain NPCs would fall silent after interactions.
[*] Reduced Scrap Value to balance the economy. Apologies to our scrappers!

notes.title: An Update to the Antivirus-Situation
notes.notes:
We’re making progress on getting beyond.frontiers unflagged as a false positive, and we’ve got some good news to share! 

[b][url=https://forums.malwarebytes.com/topic/317496-beyondfrontiers-false-positive-genheuripz6/]Malwarebytes[/url][/b] (forum Topic) and [b]Bitdefender/Emsisoft[/b] (per mail) have both responded positively and swiftly, clearing the game from their lists of flagged files. We're grateful for their professionalism and prompt handling of the situation.

However, we’re still waiting on responses from a few others. Companies like [b]Arcabit[/b], [b]BKav Pro[/b], [b]CTX[/b], [b]eScan[/b], [b]GData[/b], [b]MaxSecure[/b], [b]Panda[/b], [b]Trellix HX[/b], and [b]Vipre[/b] have received our sample files along with source code insights to help speed up the process, and we’re hopeful that they’ll follow suit soon.

Please allow at least one Definition update for your antivirus-program to stop flagging the game.

[b]Arcabit[/b] has been impossible to contact for now, if someone knows the correct address or has contacts there, please reach out to us at press[at]beyondfrontiers.eu

Now, we can’t forget about the hero of the hour—an unnamed antivirus company that turned our request to fix a false positive into a dazzling sales pitch. Apparently, instead of simply acknowledging that their software flagged our game as malware and investigating how their "Bleeding Edge AI Scanning", they thought it was a great opportunity to try and sell us an "enterprise protection package" as the only way to whitelist beyond.frontiers. For now, we’ve kindly declined, as our budget is tight better spent on making beyond.frontiers even better.

Thanks again to all of you for your continued patience and trust during this process. We know this can be frustrating, but we’re confident everything will be resolved soon. Stay tuned for updates, and in the meantime, keep exploring the stars!

- The Duality Beyond Studios Team

notes.title: beyond.frontiers launches into Early Access on November 11th, 2024
notes.notes:
[b]beyond.frontiers Launches into Early Access on November 11th, 2024[/b]

Commanders, we have a bittersweet announcement to share. [b]On November 11th, 2024[/b], [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] will officially enter Steam Early Access at a reduced price of [b]$9.99[/b] (instead of the original [i]$14.99[/i]). While this brings us closer to you experiencing the galaxy we've been crafting, it also comes with the acknowledgment that the game isn't yet the polished product we envisioned.

We had hoped to release [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] as a fully realized game, with all the rich storylines and refined mechanics in place. However, as development has progressed, it has become clear that we simply need more time. Early Access is a step we didn’t initially plan on taking, but we feel it is the best course of action to ensure that [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] meets the high standard you deserve.

[b]Why Early Access?[/b]

Our team remains committed to creating an unforgettable space adventure, but continuing development at the level of quality we strive for requires more than just time — it requires additional resources. Early Access will give us the opportunity to gather vital feedback from you, the players, while allowing us to sustain our studio financially. By releasing into Early Access, we will be able to fund essential tasks such as commissioning new [i]artists[/i] and expanding our [i]voice acting[/i] cast, helping us bring the universe of [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] to life in the most immersive way possible.

This wasn’t an easy decision for us. We truly wanted the game to be complete before putting it in your hands. Rest assured, however, that we are working to keep the Early Access period as short as possible. Our goal is to have [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] fully released within a year, at the very latest. Until then, your feedback will be vital in helping us improve the game, and we encourage you to share your thoughts and reactions with us. Let’s make this game the best it can be — together.

[b]A Personal Note from Dex, Lead Developer[/b]

I wanted to take a moment to share something personal with you all. The development of [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] has been an incredible journey, but it hasn't always been easy. For a long time, this project has been sustained by the generous support of our valued Patreons, and also by my own disability money. It's been a labor of love—made possible through sheer passion, determination, and the amazing community that has rallied around us. 

Your support means the world, and it's because of you that we've come this far. Thank you for believing in *beyond.frontiers* and helping us reach for the stars.

[b]What’s next?[/b]

To help you experience what we’re building, we will be delivering a [b]FREE demo[/b] of [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] over the coming weeks, that will unlock extra content in the main Game. This demo will give you a taste of what’s to come, and we’re aiming to participate in [b]Steam Next Fest[/b] so that you can dive deeper into our galaxy. Stay tuned for more details on that!

Although [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] will launch in Early Access, please understand that this is just the beginning. Over the coming months, we’ll be releasing frequent updates to the game, expanding the universe with new ships, more storylines, refined mechanics, and even features like station-building.

While we wish we could have offered you the complete game right away, we are confident that with your feedback, we can make [i]beyond.frontiers[/i] the space epic we've always dreamed of. Thank you for your support, your patience, and for helping us shape the future of the game.

We'll see you among the stars, Commanders. November 11th marks just the beginning.

[i]— The Team at Duality Beyond Studios[/i]

The addition of a minimap and discoverable galaxy map aids navigation, while equipment rarity introduces a new layer of strategy. We’ve also added savegame functionality, a diverse array of new ships and ship classes, and new sectors filled with fog and nebulae. Accompanying these new vessels are three distinct ship classes: the Freelancer/Courier class for those who prefer independence and speed, the Pirate class designed for those who thrive on risk and plunder, and the Defender class for pilots focused on protection and tactical superiority.
